body:
The fact that a `RefCounted` can't be referenced again once the refcount reaches zero is fundamental and shouldn't be fought against. If we ever have a way to have `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` work on `RefCounted` derivatives, it must achieve so at a different level.

The main point here is that once the reference count has reached zero, the object may be in any state from being about to be freed to being already freed. In other words, it's a use-after-free bug trying to do anything with the object from that point, including trying to reference it again.

The test case in this PR can get by because if fails to comply with the contract of `unreference()`, by which you should free the object if it returns `true` (which happens if that call to `unreference()` made the refcount reach 0).

I did have this concern before but I now believe this is perfectly fine.

By receiving such a special count-zero `RefCounted`  instance, a `Variant` can assume that `RefCounted` has finished its reference counting duty (will never revive again by any means, guaranteed by its implementation) and someone responsible for freeing it wants to do extra things with `Variant` before freeing it. It is caller's duty to provide an object that has not been freed (if it is use-after-free, the functions crash anyway regardless of this PR).

The contract of `RefCounted` is that the final owner is responsible for freeing it.  As in this case `Variant` does not own this object for the arguement we made above, it can just view it as a normal object and do what it does to a normal object.

> Documentation should be added to RefCounted and/or `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` and `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE_CLEANUP` symbols to clarify this exception to the `RefCounted`'s normal behavior

Users of `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` should feel no difference of `RefCounted` from other classes, and as a common knowledge they shouldn't cache any of them at all, it is not just `RefCounted`. But I think I should note in the doc that if deletion is canceled  a `RefCounted` must be manually freed.

I remember stumbling across this issue a while back, but I mostly worked around it.

So I was a bit surprised to find that the documentation tutorial for [the compositor](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/rendering/compositor.html) uses `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE`:

```gd
# System notifications, we want to react on the notification that
# alerts us we are about to be destroyed.
func _notification(what):
	if what == NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE:
		if shader.is_valid():
			# Freeing our shader will also free any dependents such as the pipeline!
			rd.free_rid(shader)
```

And this code *does* seem to work properly, although I'm a bit confused as to how (I assume this behavior is specific to how GDScript handles function calls, and might not work in other scripting languages).

However, I can confirm that `self` is null:

```gd
			print("self = ", self)
			print("shader = ", shader)
```
```
self = <Object#null>
shader = RID(10075993276995)
```

And calling any methods results in an error.

So in a more complex scenario, this could be a problem.

The solution in this PR makes sense to me. Essentially, treating refcount 0 objects as plain ol `Object` types with the presumption that we're in the middle of a memdelete.
unfortunately in debug builds `<Object#null>` is a previously freed object, and does not equal 'null', or cause a crash..
